Town Council Meeting                       October 27, 2026                                  Page 1 of 3Page 1

Item 7.1




Date: October 27, 2026

Honorable Mayor and Council Members:

Author and title: Erin Brewster, Sustainability Program Manager

Title:   Heat Pump Air Conditioning Rebate Program Guidelines

Jen Callaway, Town Manager

Recommended Action: That Council:
   (1) Approves the guidelines for the Heat Pump Air Conditioning Rebate Program and provides
       direction to staff on recommended program goals and performance metrics.
   (2) Approves staff’s recommendation to include costs for an online application tool in the program
       budget.
   (3) Authorizes staff to utilize the full approved Fiscal Year 26/27 budget of $70,000 from CIP C2611
       to support both the proposed heat pump air conditioning rebates and the existing Truckee Donner
       Public Utility District weatherization rebate partnership, with flexibility to allocate funds as needed
       across both rebate programs on a first-come, first-served basis.

Program Goal: Reduce greenhouse gas emissions from residential space
heating by incentivizing installation of high-efficiency electric heat pump
space heaters in Truckee homes. Specifically, this program will encourage
installation of dual-fuel heat pumps instead of air conditioning-only
equipment, as well as further incentivizing full heating system
electrification. Metrics to be used to evaluate program success include the
number of heat pump units installed, both as part of dual-fuel systems and
as replacements for gas or propane furnaces, and the percentage of
cooling equipment installed as heat pumps rather than air conditioning-
only units.

Discussion: The Town of Truckee has committed to reducing its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions 40%
by 2030, and 80% by 2040, relative to a 2008 baseline. Building energy use is the second-largest source
of community-wide GHG emissions, which are primarily from natural gas use for space heating.
Addressing this source of emissions will be a key part of meeting the Town’s adopted GHG emissions
reduction goals. The Town’s adopted Climate Action Plan identifies the need for a comprehensive
electrification and energy efficiency retrofit program (Action CAP-7.A) to address these emissions
sources. The Climate Action Plan outlines that energy efficiency initiatives are expected to achieve a
maximum reduction of 20% in existing residential energy use by 2030, with the majority of GHG emissions
reduction in this sector coming from fuel-switching initiatives such as installation of high-efficiency electric
space heating equipment to replace natural gas or propane furnaces.

During the Town’s exploration of building energy reach codes from 2022-2024, heat pump air conditioning
was identified as a key area of focus for building decarbonization efforts (see staff report linked as
Attachment 1). While air conditioning (A/C) is still relatively uncommon in Truckee, demand for air
conditioning is increasing, with 80-90% of A/C units installed in recent years representing new cooling
capacity rather than replacements of existing units. This trend is expected to continue as Truckee
experiences the impacts of climate change, presenting a time-sensitive opportunity to promote the

                                                                                                             Page 30

Item 7.1
installation of heat pumps instead of A/C-only units in Truckee. Air conditioners and heat pumps are
essentially the same type of equipment, which move heat from one place to another rather than
generating it through combustion. Heat pumps have a reversing valve that allows them to transfer heat
in both directions, providing both heating and cooling, while A/C units can only provide cooling. Instead
of installing an A/C-only unit alongside an existing gas furnace, homeowners can install a heat pump to
create a dual-fuel heating system, referred to as “heat pump air conditioning.” Heat pump air conditioning
has a much lower incremental cost compared to full heating system electrification and is likely to be more
appealing to residents who are reluctant to fully electrify their heating equipment. While dual-fuel systems
may not completely replace natural gas use for heating, they can still significantly reduce natural gas use
and associated GHG emissions from space heating.

On December 10, 2024, the Town Council directed staff to (a) develop a residential heat pump air
conditioning incentive program, (b) analyze potential policy options for a heat pump air conditioning
requirement for single-family homes in Truckee and present recommendations to the Town Council for
consideration, and (c) integrate heat pump air conditioning into contractor education programs (see
Attachment 1). Due to lack of qualified consultant availability and changes in state law, the Town did not
move forward with exploration of a heat pump air conditioning reach code in 2025, but heat pump air
conditioning and dual-fuel systems have been integrated into the contractor education program offered
by Balance Point Home Performance and Sierra Business Council beginning with a webinar in April 2026.
This report presents recommended guidelines for the heat pump air conditioning incentive program.

Proposed Rebate Program Details
This heat pump rebate program offers a base rebate available for installation of a qualifying heat pump
unit that reduces fossil fuel use for residential heating, including systems installed alongside a gas or
propane furnace as part of a dual-fuel system. A higher rebate amount is proposed for installations that
fully replace an existing gas or propane furnace, as shown in Table 1 below. Full proposed program
guidelines and equipment requirements are in Attachment 2.

                            Table 1: Proposed Town Heat Pump Rebate Amounts
                                                         Heat Pump Air               Full Heating System
                                                         Conditioning1                 Electrification2
       Base Rebate Amount                                   $2,000                          $3,000
       Additional Amount: Duct Leakage                      $1,000                          $1,000
       Testing and Mitigation
                  Maximum Total Rebate:                       $3,000                         $4,000
       1Applies to heat pumps installed to replace existing A/C units or to add new cooling capacity as part

       of a dual-fuel system with a gas or propane furnace.
       2Requires removal of existing gas or propane furnace in addition to heat pump installation to qualify.



Additionally, to improve heating and cooling efficiency and encourage right-sizing of heat pump units, an
optional additional rebate of $1,000 is available towards the cost of air duct leakage testing and mitigation
when conducted alongside an eligible heat pump installation. This additional rebate can be “stacked” with
the residential building envelope rebates offered by the Town and Truckee Donner Public Utility District
(TDPUD) for a total of up to $2,600 towards duct leakage testing and mitigation. This was added to the
proposed guidelines based on the cost-effectiveness research conducted by consultants and
conversations with local HVAC experts, who indicated that many local duct systems are in serious need
of repair or replacement. Duct leakage causes reduced system efficiency, leading to unnecessary
oversizing of equipment, and increased costs to the consumer for both equipment and energy use.
Eligible costs for this additional rebate include:
       Central system duct leakage testing (both before and after mitigation measures)
       Duct sealing and repairs or mitigation of other issues identified during duct leakage tests


                                                                                                                Page 31

Item 7.1
          Duct replacement

The heat pump rebates are designed to stack with TDPUD’s existing heat pump rebates when applicable,
increasing the total potential rebates available to Truckee residents. A typical dual-fuel heat pump system
will switch over to gas heat at an outdoor temperature of around 35-40 degrees. With these settings, a
dual-fuel system would not be eligible for TDPUD rebates, which require that backup gas heat only
operates at 20F or below. However, homeowners could size their dual-fuel heat pumps to take on a larger
share of the heating load and receive up to $1,750 in additional incentives from TDPUD, with the total
applicable rebate depending on equipment size and efficiency ratings. TDPUD offers higher rebate
amounts for full heating system electrification, which results in the following tiered rebate structure for
eligible heat pump installations, assuming a 3-ton heat pump. These amounts do not include the optional
$1,000 for duct testing and mitigation.

                       Table 2: Total Potential Rebates for a 3-Ton Heat Pump Installation
                                                                                     TDPUD
                          Scenario                            Town Rebate                              Total Rebate
                                                                                     Rebate
    Dual-Fuel System (default settings)                            $2,000              $0                 $2,000
    Dual-Fuel System (backup heat limited to <20F)                 $2,000          $600-$1,050        $2,600-$3,050
    Full system electrification                                    $3,000         $1,500-$2,400       $4,500-$5,400

This tiered structure accomplishes the following goals, based on direction received from the Town Council
in December 2024:
      1. Offsetting the incremental cost of heat pumps compared to similarly-sized A/C-only units to
         encourage installation of dual-fuel heat pumps instead of separate furnace and A/C
      2. Incentivizing upsizing of heat pump units in dual-fuel systems to take on a larger percentage of
         the heating load
      3. Further incentivizing full system electrification

Currently, there are no available rebates from Liberty Utilities that would be possible to combine with the
proposed Town-funded rebate program, as Liberty Utilities heat pump rebates are only for replacement
of existing electric equipment. Under the current proposed guidelines, the Town-funded heat pump
rebates are only available for heat pump installations that reduce natural gas or propane use for heating.

Cost Gap Analysis
Cost analysis for heat pump upgrades and was conducted by the statewide California Energy Codes and
Standards (CECS) program using Truckee-specific data as well as additional research by two consultants
funded with a grant from the California Energy Commission. According to research conducted by
Infrastructure Improvement, Inc., the typical cost gap (after consideration of existing utility incentives) to
install a similarly sized heat pump instead of air conditioning equipment in a centrally ducted heating
system is approximately $1,400-$2,800. The proposed $2,000 rebate for heat pump air conditioning is
expected to offset the typical expected incremental equipment cost for the current average air conditioner
unit size installed in Truckee (approximately 3 tons). Because heat pumps and air conditioners are
essentially the same type of equipment, installation costs are similar when installed alongside a gas
furnace in a centrally ducted system, so only equipment cost was analyzed for this cost gap. It’s important
to note that the actual cost and cost gap for any individual HVAC project may vary significantly based on
the specifics of the home and equipment used.

Because Truckee’s heating demand is significantly higher than the cooling demand, heat pumps based
on A/C unit size will not fully cover the heating load. However, previous studies of heat pump air
conditioning in cold climates demonstrated that heat pumps sized based on existing A/C capacity covered
a larger share of the heating load than expected because the original A/C units had been oversized. 1


1

Item 7.2




Date: October 27, 2026

Honorable Mayor and Council Members:

Author and title: Melanie Grebitus, Sustainability Program Analyst II

Title:   Solid Waste Collection Services Franchise Agreement Procurement Update

Jen Callaway, Town Manager

Recommended Action: That Council: (1) receive an update on the process of developing the next
solid waste collection services franchise agreement; and (2) provide feedback on items to include in
the request for proposals (RFP).

Executive Summary: The current ten-year solid waste franchise agreement with Tahoe Truckee Sierra
Disposal (TTSD) ends on June 30, 2028, unless extended by the Town, for up to a period of one year,
which may occur up to three times. In November 2025, the Town Council authorized the Town Manager
to execute a contract with HF&H Consultants, L.L.C. (HF&H), for consultant services to develop a new
solid waste franchise agreement. Throughout 2026, Town staff and HF&H have conducted residential
and commercial engagement to inform the collection and processing services to be requested under
the next agreement. The feedback gathered, as well as recommendations from Town staff regarding
improvements and refinements to include in the next solid waste franchise agreement are summarized
in this report. After review from Town Council, Town staff and HF&H plan to issue a competitive request
for proposals (RFP) to solicit proposals from solid waste haulers for the Town’s next collection service
agreement, with the expectation that the service agreement will go into effect July 1, 2028, or July 1,
2029, if the Town chooses to exercise a one-year extension of the current agreement.

Discussion:

The Town’s current franchise agreement, which began July 1, 2018, introduced several new residential
and commercial collection and processing services to align with the regulations created by Senate Bill
(SB) 1383. These regulations went into effect January 1, 2022, and require diversion of organic
materials, including yard waste and paper products. The current agreement introduced blue carts for
recycling, green carts for yard trimmings, and food scraps collection for certain businesses. These new
programs have increased diversion of organic waste from landfills and eliminated plastic waste from
green bags and significantly reduced plastic waste from blue bags, which were the previous collection
methods for recyclables and yard trimmings.

These new collection programs have been successful in diverting required materials and have been
received well by residential and commercial customers. Town staff does not anticipate that
implementation of the next franchise agreement will involve programmatic changes to the same degree
as those experienced during the previous contract transition. However, staff recommend small
changes based on challenges observed during the current franchise agreement, feedback from
businesses and residents, and minimal changes required by state law.

A. Franchise Agreement Development Process and Timeline




                                                                                                       Page 43

Item 7.2
The current franchise agreement between the Town and TTSD ends on June 30, 2028. The Town has
the option to extend the current agreement via three one-year extensions for a total of three years. On
November 10, 2025, the Town Council authorized the Town Manager to approve a one-year extension
of the current franchise agreement with TTSD, if deemed necessary, to accommodate the timeline for
development of the next franchise agreement. At this time, staff have not yet determined if an extension
will be necessary. The Town is required to give the franchised hauler written notice 180 days before the
end of the expiration of the term. Therefore, the Town has until January 2, 2028, to notify the franchised
hauler of the intent to extend the agreement.

Town staff plan to issue a competitive RFP from solid waste haulers to ensure competitive rates and
service offerings for Truckee residents and businesses. Given TTSD’s recent announcement of its
proposed sale to Recology, TTSD will not be submitting a proposal on the Town’s next franchise
agreement if the sale is completed. Town staff and HF&H are currently reviewing TTSD’s proposal to
assign the existing franchise agreement to Recology. Town staff and HF&H’s review of the assignment
is anticipated to be brought to Town Council in November, pending receipt of requested data from
TTSD and Recology.

The process for developing the RFP and new franchise agreement began in December 2025 and
includes the following phases:

Phase 1: Public Engagement (December 2025 - October 2026)

   -   Design & Review Meetings
   -   Residential Survey & Workshop
   -   Commercial Survey & Workshop
   -   Design & Review
   -   Presentation to Town Council (October 27, 2026 Town Council Meeting)

Phase 2: Draft Request for Proposals (October 2026-February 2027)

   -   Design Intake Meetings
   -   Update Franchise Agreement
   -   Prepare Solicitation Documents
   -   Presentation to Town Council

Phase 3: Proposal Review & Negotiations (March-December 2027)

   -   Issue RFP
   -   Review Proposal(s)
   -   Proposer Interview(s)
   -   Negotiate with Finalist
   -   Presentation to Town Council

Transition Period: January – June 2028, with option to extend to June 2029, if needed, to provide time
for selected hauler to acquire equipment and resources needed to implement services required in the
contract, which can sometimes take up to one year.

B. Summary of Public Engagement

Commercial Outreach
In March 2026, the Town hosted four workshops with the business community to receive feedback on
commercial collection services, including two general business workshops, one meeting with downtown
businesses, and one meeting with large businesses and agencies. Representatives from nearly 30
businesses participated. Town staff shared the process of developing the next solid waste agreement,
and businesses shared feedback on collection services specifically provided to businesses. A
commercial survey was also conducted in March through April to invite open-ended feedback on
